title: Evidence Outline
description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–1098). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Part IX covers expert bases and reliability (703, 705, Frye, Daubert, Joiner, Kumho Tire). Part X covers authentication and the best evidence rule (901–902, 1001–1008). Part XI covers Rule 501, the psychotherapist and lawyer-client privileges, 502 waiver, government lawyers, and self-incrimination. Part XII covers the spousal and marital-confidences privileges. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

title: Professional Responsibility Outline
description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Burk, Ethical Lawyering, Chs. 1–25, and the Model Rules with their Comments), in syllabus order. Part I covers regulating lawyers: sources of law, bar admission and discipline, unauthorized practice, the consequences of misconduct, and why smart people do stupid things. Part II covers the MR 1.0 definitions, competence and diligence, the duty of care and ineffective assistance, forming the relationship, scope, duties to non-clients, clients with decision-making limitations (MR 1.14), and declining and withdrawing. Part III covers confidentiality, privilege and work product, and the MR 1.6(b) exceptions. Part IV covers the lawyer as fiduciary and agent, candor under MR 1.4, and the allocation of authority. Part V covers fees, retainers, fee sharing, and trust accounts. Part VI covers conflicts: personal-interest conflicts under MR 1.8, concurrent and former clients, imputation and screening, and consent. Part VII covers government lawyers, the revolving door (MR 1.11, 1.12), and prosecutors (MR 3.8). Part VIII covers ethics in advocacy (MR 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.9). Part IX covers supervision in law firms, selling a practice, and organizational clients (MR 1.13). Part X covers public service (MR 6.1–6.5). Part XI covers truthfulness, represented and unrepresented persons, client wrongdoing, threats and reporting, restrictions on practice, and advertising and solicitation. Part XII covers MR 8.4(g), and Part XIII has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, the class quiz answers for Chs. 22, 24, and 25 worked in, and case cards for the cases the readings rely on, including the assigned Bradwell and Zauderer.

description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus, in syllabus order. The syllabus assigns the 15th edition of Prosser, Wade & Schwartz; the outline follows the 13th edition and maps each reading to its 13th-ed. chapter and cases. Part I covers the move from strict liability to fault. Parts II and III cover intent, battery, assault, false imprisonment, IIED, trespass to land and chattels, conversion, and the privileges: consent, self-defense, defense of others and of property, recapture, the shopkeeper's privilege, necessity, and discipline. Parts IV and V cover the negligence case, the Hand formula, the reasonable person, professionals and informed consent, negligence per se, notice, and res ipsa loquitur. Part VI covers but-for and substantial-factor causation, lost chance, alternative and market share liability, proximate cause, and superseding causes. Part VII covers duty and the failure to act. Part VIII covers comparative fault, assumption of risk, limitations, and immunities. Parts IX through XIV cover premises liability, damages, joint and several liability and contribution, vicarious liability, strict liability, and nuisance, and Part XV has review tables for the final. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a case card for each principal case in the assigned pages. The Canvas-only readings are not briefed.

title: Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions
description: The Restatement (Third) of Torts: Miscellaneous Provisions sections the outline relies on, from Tentative Draft No. 3 (2024). Statutes of limitations and repose (§§ 1–16), aiding and abetting negligence, agreements to act negligently, the firefighter's rule, and liability for providing alcohol come with their black letter, Comments, and Illustrations. The Sections the ALI approved in 2022 come as black letter: apportionment (§§ 4 A–4 B and 27–37), immunities (§§ 1–10A), and loss of consortium (§§ 48 A–48 C). Search by word or section number, filter by outline topic, and open or close the Comments.
